answers.note: Solid concrete-to-written modelling with an explicit swap of ten ones and a hinge check with a reteach threshold, but practice is mostly a list of exchange sums with no no-exchange-to-exchange progression or real reasoning task.

Excellent CPA sequence with explicit exchange language, diagnostic hinge questions with clear next steps, and varied practice (exchange/no-exchange sort, faded examples, reasoning and missing-digit tasks), all maths and timings correct.
Strong CPA teaching, whiteboard guided check and tiered, varied practice, but the challenge missing-digit item is left half-corrected with an impossible original version in the text.

Accurate Milgram content and a well-scaffolded PEEL evaluation workshop with a model and card sort, but the 6-mark exam question has only a PEEL checklist rather than guidance on how the marks are earned.

Clear PEEL frame and an 8-mark question with a mark scheme, but omits the Yale setting, its ethics MCQ has two defensible answers (deception and right to withdraw), and protection from harm and right to withdraw are not properly taught.
Outstanding explicit teaching of an evaluation chain with I do/we do/you do and good and broken models, though students never attempt the referenced 16-mark question in the lesson.
Logical, kit-based sequence with retrieval starters every week, a baseline torch drawing repeated at the end, a matching end quiz and practical, and clear primary safety rules.

A thin but sensible sequence with retrieval starters, but it gives no mains-electricity safety message, its starting check is only an unrecorded oral question, and it teaches that series bulbs 'share the electricity'.

Detailed plan with good safety and a baseline and end quiz, but week 1 has no kit-based practical, most starters introduce new content rather than retrieve, and it teaches Year 6 circuit symbols and lists 'all metals are conductors' as a misconception.
